name: Weyerhaeuser
old_description: We use trees to make products people need while taking care of forests for future generations
about:
Weyerhaeuser operates from Heaters, West Virginia, where it manages timberlands and produces wood products. The company describes its history as "More Than a Century of Expertise," though a specific founding year is not provided in the available information. Ownership structure and founder names are not disclosed in the source material.

The company’s operations span sustainable forest management, wood products manufacturing, land and mineral resource management, and climate solutions. Its wood products segment supplies value-added solutions such as framing components, architectural wood doors, windows, and millwork, marketed under brands like Trus Joist. The land and minerals division provides building blocks for real estate, development, and conservation, while the climate solutions group pursues renewable energy development, forest carbon sequestration, carbon capture and storage, and conservation and mitigation banking.

Weyerhaeuser serves the construction and building materials industries, including residential and commercial framing, architectural millwork, and engineered wood products. It also works with real estate developers, conservation organizations, and renewable energy projects. The company’s distribution network includes local partners that stock Trus Joist products, and it offers regional product documentation and service information.

The company states its purpose as using trees to make products people need while taking care of forests for future generations. It differentiates itself through long-term forest stewardship, integration of climate solutions with traditional forest products, and community investment programs such as the Thrive initiative, which recently committed $1 million to Drayton Valley, Alberta.

name: What Chefs Want!
old_description: Your trusted partners for chef-curated ingredients. Dynamic service with daily delivery, no minimums and around the clock support, built to help chefs succeed.
about:
What Chefs Want is headquartered in Lexington, Kentucky, with significant operations in Louisville. The company was founded by Ron Turnier, who serves as CEO, though a founding year is not publicly disclosed. The business began as a chef-centered wholesale distributor focused on eliminating traditional friction points in foodservice procurement.

The company operates as a broadline food distributor across 12 states — Alabama, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Missouri, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, and Tennessee — running 19 distribution centers that serve over 16,000 restaurants. Its seven core product lines span produce, seafood, meat, gourmet, staples, to-go, and dairy. In 2026, What Chefs Want acquired Florida-based Quality Cut Produce, adding a state-of-the-art fresh-cut processing facility and expanding its PrepKitchen operation to provide pre-portioned, ready-to-use fruits and vegetables. The distributor offers daily delivery on a six-day schedule, split-case ordering, no minimum order requirements, and 24/7 customer support via phone, text, chat, and email, all backed by a proprietary web ordering platform and mobile app.

Customers include independent restaurants, multi-unit chains, schools, healthcare facilities, hospitality groups, and retail outlets. The company’s Local Food Connection and Boat Direct programs highlight a focus on regional sourcing and direct-from-harvest seafood.

What Chefs Want positions its model on operational flexibility: removing minimums, enabling split cases, and guaranteeing rapid replenishment so chefs can order precisely what they need, reduce waste, and maintain menu creativity without inventory burden. The Quality Cut acquisition was framed as a natural extension of that vision, adding production capacity to further cut prep labor and improve consistency for foodservice operators.

about:
White Space operates from Reno, Nevada, and has spent two decades turning high-stakes hospitality visions into reality. The company has delivered projects for brands such as Ritz‑Carlton, Disney, Kate Spade, Soho House, and Outrigger across locations from New York to Tel Aviv, California to Hawaii.

The firm manages the global manufacturing of custom interiors for hospitality and commercial spaces. Its services span procurement, factory‑matched production, on‑site quality control, custom furniture design, millwork, stone and glass fabrication, and full installation. White Space reports 600‑plus furniture designs completed and a 99 % customer satisfaction rate, with a team of project and QC managers overseeing production at partner factories worldwide.

Clients come from the hospitality, gaming, luxury resort, and restaurant sectors. Concrete examples include the Cosmopolitan Las Vegas, Hyatt Miraval, the George, and Soho House Jaffa. The company also serves commercial developers and architects seeking turnkey interior execution.

White Space differentiates itself by building a purpose‑built supply chain for each project, providing US‑based project management with boots‑on‑the‑ground quality teams at every factory. The company emphasizes masterful millwork and complex architectural woodwork as core expertise, and promises standards without borders through direct oversight of production and logistics.

name: White Wolf Custom Apparel
old_description: Next Level Custom Apparel and Promotional Items for Businesses and Beyond
about:
White Wolf Custom Apparel is a family-owned custom apparel and promotional products shop based in Little Falls, Minnesota. The company serves businesses, teams, and events across Central Minnesota, including Brainerd, St. Cloud, Little Falls, Sartell, Sauk Rapids, and surrounding communities. The shop describes itself as built for brands that refuse to blend in, moving fast and delivering like a powerhouse while maintaining a family-owned approach.

The shop provides custom embroidery, screen printed transfers, laser engraving, custom hat patches, promotional products, and online merch stores. Production is 90% in-house with no minimum order requirements. They also offer UV printing, custom drinkware, decals, and signage, handling materials such as metal, wood, glass, leather, and acrylic for laser engraving.

Customers include businesses, schools, sports teams, organizations, contractors, and fundraisers. Concrete examples include the St. Cloud State Huskies, for whom they are a proud partner, and local companies throughout Brainerd, Baxter, St. Cloud, Little Falls, Sartell, and Sauk Rapids. They outfit everyone from single-person orders to entire crews.

White Wolf emphasizes no minimums, fast turnaround, family-owned roots, 90% in-house production, premium apparel brands, local customer service, and full-service custom branding. They say they help brands turn heads, build recognition, and actually represent who they are, with high-quality custom apparel done in-house for speed, consistency, and results.

name: Whittier Wood Products
old_description: Timeless design combines with superb functionality to make your bedroom a haven.
about:
Whittier Wood Products traces its roots to 1867 when Charles Whittier joined the E.L. Brackett Lumber and Coal Company in Farmington, Minnesota, but the modern business began in 1975 when Gordon Whittier purchased a wood component manufacturing facility in Eugene, Oregon. Gordon brought in his son-in-law Evert to expand the operation, establishing a family-owned and operated enterprise that continues today under third-generation leadership, including Scott Whittier, his daughter Anna Tower, and Daniel Marshall.

The company produces solid wood furniture for bedrooms, home offices, living rooms, and media centers, marketed under collections such as Addison, Bailey, McKenzie, and Virginia. Operations span wood component manufacturing, assembly, and finishing at its Eugene factory, supplemented by a production facility opened in Vietnam in 2006. The product line includes both ready-to-finish kits sold to home centers and discount chains, and finished furniture distributed through traditional and specialty solid-wood retailers.

Whittier serves a range of B2B customers, from mass-market home centers and discount chains to unfinished furniture stores and traditional furniture retailers. Historical accounts note early contracts with department stores such as Macy’s for ready-to-assemble oak tables and cabinets. Today the company focuses on wholesale distribution to retail partners rather than direct-to-consumer sales.

The firm emphasizes heritage craftsmanship and the use of highest-grade lumber, values the family describes as honesty, integrity, and passion. Multi-generational continuity — now spanning three generations — is presented as a core differentiator, with the company highlighting its “real wood, real quality” philosophy and domestic-and-overseas manufacturing footprint.

name: Wholesale Electric Supply Co., Inc.
about:
Wholesale Electric Supply Co., Inc. was founded in 1947 in Texarkana, Texas by Amos McCulloch. The family-owned business, now led by President Buddy McCulloch, is headquartered in Fort Smith, Arkansas. It operates more than 85 branches across Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Kansas, Missouri, and Tennessee, serving customers nationwide.

The company distributes a broad range of electrical products including lighting, power distribution and switchgear, safety technology, wire and cable, cable management and raceway, and power connection and control equipment. It supports customers with vendor managed inventory programs, 24-hour emergency service, and knowledgeable personnel specializing in switchgear, lighting, hazardous locations, and data communications. The branch network enables timely and accurate material delivery across residential, commercial, and industrial projects.

Wholesale Electric Supply serves residential builders and buyers with design assistance for single-family, town-home, and multi-family dwellings. In the commercial sector, it supplies lighting, power distribution, and safety technology for various projects. Industrial customers rely on the company for switchgear, hazardous-location products, and data communications infrastructure to keep operations running.

The company emphasizes a mission of providing materials timely and accurately with an appreciative attitude, summarized by its "Yes, We Can!" philosophy. It differentiates itself through long-standing manufacturer relationships, a large branch footprint, and specialized expertise in switchgear, lighting, and hazardous locations.

name: Why Free Solar Company
old_description: Solar Specialists in Maryland – Save with Incentives + Local Service
about:
Why Free Solar Company operates from Forest Heights, Maryland, serving homeowners and businesses across Maryland, the District of Columbia, Virginia, and Pennsylvania. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm specializes in turnkey solar photovoltaic installations with $0-down financing options that leverage the 30% federal tax credit, Maryland Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs), and net metering programs. In addition to panel installation, it offers Tesla PowerWall battery storage, tree removal and roof repair for qualifying homes, and a 25-year gutter-to-gutter warranty. The company reports having served more than 10,000 customers in the National Harbor area and surrounding counties.

Its primary customers are residential property owners and commercial clients seeking to reduce electricity costs and gain energy independence. Service coverage extends to every Maryland county, including Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Montgomery, and Prince George's, as well as Northern Virginia, the District of Columbia, and parts of Pennsylvania.

Why Free Solar Company emphasizes transparent education over aggressive sales, positioning itself as a guide to help homeowners understand how incentives can make solar effectively free to install. Its stated differentiators include a performance guarantee, start-saving-from-day-one pricing, and battery backup for outage resilience.

name: Wicked Apparel
old_description: Wicked Apparel – Your Design on Quality Apparel – Made Wicked Easy
about:
Wicked Apparel operates from Manchester, New Hampshire. The company's copyright notice dates to 2014, marking its presence in the custom apparel market. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The shop specializes in screen printing and embroidery on a range of garments including t-shirts, sweatshirts, polo shirts, dress shirts, hats, and bags. It also builds and manages online fundraising stores, handling order processing and fulfillment so clients can sell custom apparel directly to their audiences. The company describes itself as a one-stop shop for decorated apparel with integrated e-commerce.

Its customer base spans local businesses, sports teams, schools, and non-profit organizations across New Hampshire. Named clients include Northeastern Sheet Metal, Inc., a sheet metal fabricator; Shuttles Auto Sales, an automotive dealership; Covenant Fire Protection, a fire safety contractor; and Mill City Energy, an energy sector firm.

Wicked Apparel emphasizes competitive pricing, fast turnaround times, and a do-it-yourself online design tool as key differentiators. The company states that quality, cost, and customer service come first, aiming to let clients focus on their core operations while it handles branding and apparel logistics.
